title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: identifying the internal transfer that funded a certificate of deposit
content:
## Scope

This rule applies to a Savings & Money Market Accounts account from which the owner funded a certificate of deposit by internal transfer, when an excess withdrawal fee on that transfer is reviewed. It fixes which withdrawal is the funding transfer and which certificate it funded.

## Policy clause

1. **The funding transfer** is the most recent withdrawal on this savings account posted as an internal transfer, taken only when its counterparty is a certificate of deposit held by the same customer.
2. **The certificate** is that counterparty: the certificate the transfer funded.
3. **Nothing identified.** When the most recent internal transfer went to any other account, nothing is refunded under this rule.
4. **One transfer on that date.** The funding transfer is taken only when exactly one internal-transfer withdrawal posted on that most recent date. When two or more did, the records do not show which one is the most recent, and nothing is refunded under this rule.

## Basis of decision

- **Authority.** The withdrawal, its channel, its counterparty and its posted date come from the savings account's transaction record; whether the counterparty is a certificate of the same customer comes from the bank's certificate records.
- **Object correlation.** Only the single most recent internal-transfer withdrawal of this savings account is looked at; an earlier internal transfer is not taken in its place.

## Input, judgement, output (hypothetical dates)

| Most recent internal-transfer withdrawal | Counterparty | Funding transfer? |
|---|---|---|
| transfer of 3 April | a certificate of deposit of the same customer | yes; that certificate is the one it funded |
| transfer of 9 April, after a certificate was funded on 3 April | the owner's checking account | no; the most recent internal transfer went to another account, so nothing is refunded under this rule |
| two internal transfers on 3 April, one to a certificate and one to checking | different accounts | no; the records do not show which is the most recent, so nothing is refunded under this rule |

Withdrawals that are not internal transfers, such as online transfers to another bank or ATM withdrawals, are never the funding transfer.

## Points of judgement

**The owner funded a certificate on 3 April and then moved money to checking by internal transfer on 9 April. Is the 3 April transfer the funding transfer?** No; the rule looks only at the most recent internal transfer, which went to checking, so nothing is refunded under this rule.

**Must the certificate still be of a particular status?** The rule asks only that the counterparty be a certificate of deposit held by the same customer.
